subject.title: [Bug]: exec tool treats subprocess nonzero exit codes as tool failures, masking stdout and exit-code semantics

question: Should completed exec results with nonzero exit codes be nonfatal agent results by default across embedded-agent and isolated cron surfaces?
rationale: Current main has two competing semantics: the exec runner preserves normal nonzero exits as completed output, while shared agent and cron state still treat the nonzero exitCode as a generic tool failure.

options.title: Make normal exec nonzero nonfatal
options.body: Update the shared classifier and cron/embedded-agent tests so completed exec exit codes preserve output and diagnostics without setting tool failure state.

options.title: Add explicit accepted-exit policy
options.body: Keep current default failure semantics but add a documented accepted-exit or nonfatal-exit policy surface, accepting added config and upgrade complexity.

options.title: Keep failure semantics
options.body: Document wrapper-based workarounds and accept that cron jobs using exit codes semantically must force exit 0 to avoid failed tool state.

recommendation.title: Make normal exec nonzero nonfatal
recommendation.body: Update the shared classifier and cron/embedded-agent tests so completed exec exit codes preserve output and diagnostics without setting tool failure state.

likelyOwner.reason: The open decision sits at the shared tool-result classifier boundary introduced in PR 93228, and that history points to steipete as the best current routing candidate.
